## Which grab this is

**This is grab 1 — a genuine pre-publish baseline.** The newest published version on
record predates today, and no publish-signature server-error spike is visible. Every
number below is from a build that is still live at freeze time.

If the update ships later today, `2026-09-04` becomes a blended day and must not be
used as a before or an after; the first day that genuinely tests the update is
`2026-09-05`.

## What this baseline can and cannot answer

| Signal | First honest read | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Script errors, crashes, server errors | immediately | event-stamped, no aggregation |
| Concurrents | immediately | but a publish restarts servers — expect a dip |
| Client crash **rate** | 2026-09-05 | daily metric; today's is dominated by pre-update hours |
| DAU, revenue, session length, playtime | 2026-09-05 | daily, UTC-bucketed |
| **D1 retention** | **2026-09-06** | D1 for 09-04 needs 09-05 to finish, plus pipeline |
| D7 retention | 2026-09-12 | same reason, longer cohort |
| D30 retention | 2026-10-05 | same |
| RFY ranking signals | 2026-09-05 | daily, and they carry **no** maturation lag |

**An absent measurement is not a clean bill of health.** Any row without data on the
follow-up is marked NO DATA, never OK.

Life history used: **71 settled days** of
`DailyActiveUsers`, from the lifetime grab of 2026-09-03/04 topped up on 2026-09-04.
Metrics with a shorter horizon — the RFY set starts 2026-05-01 on every game; crash and
performance age out at ~30 days, `ErrorCount` at ~56 — have their percentile computed
over the span that exists, not over the game's life. The `Life range` column is only as
long as the metric itself.

Values are the unbroken-down headline series (a bare `Place` filter still counts as
total; a population filter does not). Partial intervals are excluded. Where a metric's
last settled day is earlier than 2026-09-03, the *as-of* column says so — that is
maturation lag, not missing data.

## Four things that look like breakage and are not

Check all four before escalating anything above.

1. **The publish server-error spike.** A deploy day spikes `ErrorCount` `LogSource: Server`
   20-50x and clears within 24h. It is the publish, not the build. Only a finding if
   **still** elevated on 2026-09-05.
2. **The restart dip in concurrents.** A publish cycles every server. Compare against the
   day's own pre-publish slope, not yesterday's peak.
3. **Today's partial point.** 2026-09-04 is in progress and reads low. Never compare a
   partial day to a full one.
4. **Version adoption.** Error counts climb while servers cycle. Rate per player, not raw
   count, and give it 2-3 hours.

## Preferred test — split by PlaceVersion, not before/after

During the adoption overlap both builds run on the same day, same traffic mix, same
event calendar. Holding the window fixed and splitting by `PlaceVersion` attributes a
difference in a way a day-over-day delta cannot. Supported on `ClientCrashRate15m`,
`ClientCrashCount`, `ClientFpsP10`, `ClientMemoryUsagePercentageAvg`,
`OomUnexpectedExits`, `SessionDurationSecondsAvg`.

Also: **onset vs exposure.** A movement starting before any player could be served the
new build cannot have been initiated by it. Date the first *served* version, not the ship.
